mgr-001.front: Name the 6 kinds of grouse you can hunt in BC.
mgr-001.back: Ruffed, spruce, dusky (Interior), sooty (coast), sharp tailed, and ptarmigan (3 kinds). (85%)

mgr-003.front: Ruffed grouse: middle tail feather length for a male?
mgr-003.back: About 15 cm (6 in) or more. Under 14 cm (5.5 in): female. In between: use another clue. (70%)

mgr-004.front: Young of the year or adult: which feathers do you check?

mgr-006.back: Black throat and breast edged white, red comb over the eye, black tail. Franklin's form: white spots above the tail. (80 to 85%)

mgr-007.front: Why is the spruce grouse called the fool hen?
mgr-007.back: It trusts its camouflage and often lets people walk close. (80%)

mgr-046.front: A grouse flushes and glides into a fir. What now?
mgr-046.back: Mark the tree and walk straight to it, ready for a second flush. (Tip)

mgr-047.front: Bird disappears under a lone evergreen?
mgr-047.back: Circle the tree: it may walk out and flush from the far side. (Tip)

mgr-048.front: Hen ruffed grouse with chicks: what does she do?
mgr-048.back: Hisses, fans tail and ruff, may fake a broken wing to lead you away. (70%)

mgr-049.front: How does a ruffed grouse drum?
mgr-049.back: Stands on a log and beats cupped wings against the air. The wings never hit the log. (85%)

mgr-050.front: When do ruffed grouse drum most?
mgr-050.back: Spring, March to May; peak in April in one study. A little in fall too. (75 to 85%)

mgr-051.front: How far can you hear a drum?
mgr-051.back: About 400 m or more in thick woods, depending which way the bird faces. (60 to 70%)

mgr-052.back: Deep hoots with neck air sacs showing (reddish purple), yellow orange comb. Heard up to about 400 m. (75%)

mgr-053.back: Struts with red combs up and tail fanned; short flight ending in two loud wing claps. (65 to 75%)

mgr-054.back: Dawn dance on a lek: stamping feet, rattling tail, pink neck sacs. Lek calls carry up to 1.5 km. (85%)

mgr-055.back: 7 to 12 eggs, 23 to 24 days, hatch usually early June. (85%)
